findings.title: slice(1, limit + 1) drops the first (newest) row of every page
findings.explanation: Arrays are zero-indexed, so rows.slice(1, limit + 1) skips rows[0] and returns only limit-1 rows when more exist (and limit-1 or fewer on the last page). Every page silently loses its first invoice; for a page that has exactly one row, the result is empty. Use rows.slice(0, limit). Combined with next_before taken from the last element of the page, the skipped invoices are never returned on any later page either, since the cursor is id < last id. This is data loss for users.

findings.title: page[page.length - 1] can be undefined / wrong when hasMore is true
findings.explanation: With the off-by-one slice, if limit is 1, hasMore can be true while page is empty, so page[page.length - 1].id throws a TypeError and the request returns 500. Fixing the slice to slice(0, limit) resolves this, since page then always has limit >= 1 rows when hasMore is true. Also ensure limit is validated to be >= 1.

findings.title: limit + 1 bypasses any max-limit clamp semantics and needs validation
findings.explanation: The query now fetches limit + 1 rows. Confirm that limit is parsed as an integer, clamped to a sane maximum and minimum (>= 1) before this point; otherwise a value such as a string, NaN, or a huge number makes limit + 1 produce string concatenation ('10' + 1 = '101') or an unexpectedly large query. Make sure the limit is a number, not a string from req.query.

findings.title: No tests covering pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: This bug class (off-by-one at page edges) is exactly what tests catch. Add tests for: fewer than limit rows, exactly limit rows (next_before must be null), limit + 1 rows (next_before set to the id of the limit-th row, and the next page starts at the next invoice with no gaps or duplicates), and an empty result.

findings.title: Clarify naming and add a short comment
findings.explanation: Add a comment explaining that limit + 1 rows are fetched as a lookahead to detect another page, and consider naming the query parameter/variable (e.g. fetchLimit) so the intent is obvious to future readers.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
